newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares fall on domestic selling.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares fall on domestic selling.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Thursday as some domestic investors trimmed their positions in B shares in a bid to increase their investment in the hot A share market, brokers said.
The B share index ended down 0.60 points, or 0.67 percent, at 89.03, with turnover expanding to HK$18.14 million from HK$8.19 million on Wednesday.

"The A share market has been so bullish over the past few sessions that some domestic investors have liquidated part of their B share positions to divert funds over to the A shares," said Hu Xugang, a broker at China Southern Securities.
"Unless there is positive news, the B share index is likely to gradually edge lower in the coming sessions because of Thursday's decline coupled with expanded turnover," another broker said.
A broker at Shanghai Guotai Securities said falls in B shares on Thursday were linked to a sharp drop in Tsann Kuen pressured by speculative selling.

Tsann Kuen, the worst performer, fell HK$0.30, or 12.50 percent, to HK$2.10 after 3,900 shares changed hands. Television tube maker SEG slid HK$0.17, or 6.32 percent, to HK$2.52 on trade of 192,700 shares.

China Marine sank HK$0.20, or 3.17 percent, to HK$6.10 on volume of 283,700 shares on profit-taking, brokers said. For the same reason, they said, Dadonghai saw the day's most active trade of 920,200 shares to slip HK$0.02 to HK$1.34.
However, Changchai and Gujing were supported by institutional demand due to investor confidence in the two firms' earnings this year, brokers said.
Changchai was up HK$0.03 at HK$5.08 on trade of 790,400 shares. Gujing, the best performer, advanced HK$0.24 to HK$5.69, with 601,700 shares traded.

The A share index surged 29.68 points, or 8.58 percent, to close at 375.59 as turnover swelled to 14.21 billion yuan from 13.38 billion yuan the previous session. The composite index climbed 26.30 points, or 8.15 percent, to finish at 348.98.

Brokers said the A share surge was fueled in part by institutional speculative demand for recently-listed Jilin Chemical. The counter soared 6.76 yuan, or 48.49 percent, to 20.70 yuan, compared with its recent offer price of 3.50 yuan.
Northeast Electric put in the strongest performance, skyrocketing 7.81 yuan, or 108.77 percent, to 14.99 yuan on volume of 23.44 million shares.
